mission: Ben loses a sparring exchange he should not have lost, and the wrongness in the Force is the reason. Open on the night a problem he has been handling privately becomes a problem someone else could see.
why_now: The wrongness has been costing Ben since the week started. Tonight is the first time it has cost him in front of another Knight.
conflict: Ben's timing fractures mid-spar when the wrongness pulls at his attention, and the Order has been treating the background disturbance as residue from recent crises. His body fails him in a way he cannot blame on the week, and he still does not want to say so aloud.
turning_point: Alone in the salle afterward, Ben runs a form through without igniting the blade and feels the wrongness steal a beat he cannot spare. He stops pretending it is fatigue.
opening_hook: Ben's guard drops a half-second late and his sparring partner's training blade catches him across the shoulder — the third time this week the wrongness in the Force has cost him a beat he should never miss
closing_hook: Luke appears in the doorway with a datapad and an expression Ben knows means a mission
emotional_trajectory: Restless unease -> frustrated isolation -> reluctant hope

stakes.personal: Ben's sense of his own Force perception — is he reliable or traumatized?
stakes.interpersonal: His distance from other Knights who do not share his concern
stakes.external: The wrongness itself — something is happening to the Force

setting: Jedi Temple, Coruscant — training salle, late evening session
sensory_details: Training sabers humming; the salle's ambient Force presence arriving a half-beat behind the rhythm Ben's body has known by reflex for years; sweat on his palms, the sound of boots on the salle floor; distant Temple corridors still carrying the foot traffic of the late shift
canon_elements_needed: Force meditation techniques and Jedi contemplative practice
Jedi Temple architecture on Coruscant, meditation chambers
Post-Abeloth era Force sensitivity and lingering disturbances
Ben Skywalker training history and Force abilities
Jedi Knight rank responsibilities and daily life circa 47 ABY

notes: Opens with a training spar so the wrongness costs Ben something concrete before any interiority names it. Ben should read as a Knight handling a private problem privately, not as a character having a character arc in public. Voice anchor: Zahn-style close third; interior voice sharp and self-deprecating, never melodramatic. Diagnostic-voice trap — he should not, in this scene, arrive at any clinical articulation of what the wrongness is. He feels it before he can name it; the 'structural, not emotional' framing is a Part 3-4 voice, earned later. If a sentence of his interiority could be lifted into a mission debrief, it is too composed for this scene. Anti-pattern: do not describe the wrongness in visual or color terms — keep it auditory and vibrational, and use one consistent metaphor for this scene (the half-beat lag in the ambient field). The sparring partner is a background character — minimal characterization, exists to provide the physical context. Temple life at this hour can surface in the edges (late-shift foot traffic, a cleaning droid, turbolift chimes in the corridor) — Coruscant is a place people live in, not only a backdrop Ben moves through.

turning_point_detail.trigger: Alone in the salle after Rendell leaves, Ben runs a form through without igniting the blade and feels the wrongness steal a beat he cannot spare — a half-second lag in the ambient Force field that disrupts muscle memory he has relied on for years.
turning_point_detail.shift: Ben stops pretending the wrongness is fatigue or week-long exhaustion. He acknowledges, internally and without words, that something structural is wrong with the Force itself, not with him — though he cannot yet articulate what or why.
turning_point_detail.cost: The cost lands on Ben's sense of his own reliability as a Force-sensitive and as a Jedi Knight. If the wrongness is external, he is not failing; if it is internal (trauma, lingering Abeloth-bleed, psychological fracture), he is. The uncertainty isolates him from other Knights who do not feel what he feels, deepening his distance from the Order.

emotional_arc.start: Restless unease — the wrongness has been tugging at Ben's attention all week, a half-beat lag he keeps attributing to fatigue or distraction.
emotional_arc.shift: Frustrated isolation — after the sparring hit, Ben moves from unease into active frustration with his own body and a sharpening awareness that he is handling this alone because no one else feels it.
emotional_arc.end: Reluctant hope — Luke's arrival suggests that Ben's private problem is about to become a shared one, and that the Order might have resources or answers. The hope is reluctant because it means admitting the wrongness aloud and losing the privacy he has been guarding.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben's guard drops a half-second late during a sparring exchange with Rendell, and Rendell's training blade catches him across the shoulder — the third time this week the wrongness has cost Ben a beat he should never miss.
key_beats.state_change: The wrongness moves from abstract background disturbance to concrete, witnessed failure. Ben has lost a sparring exchange he should not have lost, and the wrongness is the reason.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben's body registers the hit as a sharp, clean failure — not pain, but the specific sting of a mistake his reflexes should not have allowed. His instinct pushes toward action (rematch, push harder, prove it was a fluke) rather than explanation. The wrongness is pulling at his attention even as Rendell steps back, and Ben feels the lag in the ambient Force field like a note played slightly flat.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben deactivates his training saber and waves off a rematch, claiming fatigue. He keeps his tone light, offers a reason that is not quite a lie, and waits for Rendell to accept the out and leave.
key_beats.state_change: Ben chooses isolation over explanation. He does not want to say aloud what he felt, and he does not want Rendell to press. The wrongness becomes a private problem again, but now it is a private problem that has cost him in front of another Knight.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben's internal voice tightens into self-deprecation — a sharp, practiced move toward humor that deflects without lying. He feels the weight of the wrongness as isolation: Rendell does not feel it, the other Knights do not feel it, and Ben cannot explain it without sounding like he is either traumatized or unreliable. The frustration is clean and sharp, not melodramatic — a Knight's frustration with his own body.

key_beats.beat_description: Alone in the salle, Ben paces and runs through a form without igniting the blade, testing whether the wrongness disrupts muscle memory or Force timing. He moves through the sequence slowly, feeling for the half-beat lag in the ambient field, and finds it — the Force arriving a half-second behind the rhythm his body has known by reflex for years.
key_beats.state_change: The turning point lands. Ben stops pretending the wrongness is fatigue. He acknowledges, without words, that something is structurally wrong with the Force itself, not with him — though he cannot yet name what or why. The private problem becomes undeniable.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben's body moves through the form with precision, but his Force-sense registers the lag like a musician hearing a note played slightly flat. The wrongness is not in him; it is in the ambient field. The realization arrives not as a thought but as a physical sensation — a tightening in his chest, a sharpening of focus, a shift from 'I am failing' to 'something is wrong.' He does not articulate this; he feels it. The frustration deepens into something closer to dread, but Ben does not name that either.

key_beats.beat_description: Luke appears in the doorway with a datapad and mission-ready posture — the expression Ben knows means a mission is coming.
key_beats.state_change: External pressure arrives at the boundary of the scene. Ben's private problem is about to become a shared one. The Order is about to move, and Ben will have to speak aloud what he has been handling alone.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben feels a surge of reluctant hope — relief that he might not be alone with this, mixed with the cost of admitting it. The hope is reluctant because it means losing the privacy he has been guarding and stepping into whatever Luke is about to ask of him. Ben braces for the handoff, his body already shifting from the form into readiness.
